skill.name: waterfall-development
skill.description: Enforces a waterfall workflow for AI-assisted software development. Uses features.yml, phase gates, and validation checks to control phase transitions.
skill.summary: Enforces a waterfall workflow with explicit phase gates for AI-assisted software delivery.
skill.author: Chemiseblanc

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged markdown backticks, a validation loop, and one hardcoded local validation command. No evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration, network access, or command injection was found in the reviewed files.

static_findings.snippet: Strict phase gate enforcement for waterfall workflow. Requires the `feature-file` skill for artifact

finding_verdicts.reason: The flagged text is a markdown table entry showing an example file path. It is not executable Ruby or shell syntax.
The backticks only format an example TypeScript path in documentation. There is no command execution context or user-controlled shell input.
This is markdown inline code for an example application file. It does not invoke a shell or execute dynamic code.
The flagged snippet is an example test file path inside a fenced markdown example. It is documentation, not executable backtick evaluation.
The line iterates over test identifiers from the local features.yml data model. It does not inspect the host system, environment, files outside the workflow document, or network state.
The condition checks whether declared test identifiers exist in the local test-cases map. This is workflow validation, not system reconnaissance.
The backticks mark the companion skill name feature-file in prose. This is not executable code or a shell command.
The line documents a hardcoded local validation script used by the skill. The script reads features.yml and validates phase gates; no command injection, network access, or secret access was found.

content.value_statement: AI coding sessions can skip requirements, design, or testing when pressure rises. This skill keeps work inside a strict waterfall flow with documented gates.
actual_capabilities: Activates when features.yml exists or when a user requests the waterfall workflow.
Defines Requirements, Design, Implementation, Testing, and Complete phases.
Runs a local gate validator before work continues.
Blocks work that does not match the current feature phase.
Documents gate criteria and fixes for failed transitions.
Provides a blueprint format for implementation planning.
limitations: Depends on the companion feature-file skill for artifact management.
Checks declared test status, not actual test execution results.
May be too rigid for iterative or discovery-heavy projects.

use_cases.title: Control Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Keep AI-assisted feature work aligned with approved requirements, design decisions, implementation status, and testing evidence.

use_cases.title: Prepare Test Signoff
use_cases.description: Verify that every requirement has linked tests before a feature moves to Complete.

use_cases.title: Structure AI Coding Work
use_cases.description: Guide Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a predictable sequence before code changes begin.

prompt_templates.title: Start Waterfall Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the waterfall workflow for this feature. Check the current phase and tell me which gate must pass next.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for an existing feature file.

prompt_templates.title: Check Phase Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate whether my selected feature is ready to move from Design to Implementation. Report any missing gate evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Implementation Blueprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a waterfall implementation blueprint for this approved feature. Include approach, key files, steps, risks, and testing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured planning after requirements and decisions are complete.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Completion Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Before marking this feature Complete, verify all requirements, test links, and passing test flags. Stop if any gate fails.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced final review before delivery signoff.

output_examples.input: A developer asks to start coding while the feature is still in Requirements.
output_examples.output: The assistant blocks implementation and lists the missing Design gate evidence.

output_examples.input: A QA engineer asks whether a feature can move to Complete.
output: The assistant checks requirement status, tested-by links, referenced test cases, and passing flags.
It reports each failed gate before any completion action.

output_examples.input: An engineering lead asks for an implementation plan after Design approval.
output_examples.output: The assistant produces a concise blueprint with approach, key files, ordered steps, risks, dependencies, and tests.

best_practices: Keep feature requirements small, explicit, and linked to test evidence.
Run gate validation before changing phase or starting new work.
Record design decisions before implementation begins.
anti_patterns: Do not bypass a failed gate to continue coding.
Do not mark tests passing without real verification.
Do not use the workflow when rapid exploration is the primary goal.

faq.question: What does this skill enforce?
faq.answer: It enforces a waterfall flow from Requirements through Complete using documented phase gates.

faq.question: Does it create features.yml?
faq.answer: It can request creation through the companion feature-file skill when invoked without an existing file.

faq.question: Does it run my test suite?
faq.answer: No. It checks declared test links and passing flags in the feature data.

faq.question: Can it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when traceability, phase control, and explicit testing evidence matter more than speed.

faq.question: What happens when a gate fails?
faq.answer: The assistant reports the failure and stops work until the missing evidence is fixed.
